text:
Good evening, Burlington. The clouds that hung around most of the day have finally broken up, and we're getting a nice clear sunset around 4:24. It's in the low 40s now and will fall off quickly once the sun goes down. Tonight stays mostly clear and chilly, with a low around 31, so expect a little frost on the windshield and a jacket for the evening dog walk.

Tomorrow is the start of a friendlier stretch. Plenty of sunshine, a high near 51, about 7 degrees warmer than today, and a light south breeze that you won't really notice. The models are all within a couple of degrees of that number, so I'm comfortable with it. Tuesday night stays partly cloudy and milder, around 36.

Each afternoon should run a few degrees warmer than the last, with highs well into the 50s by midweek. The next real chance for showers holds off until late Sunday, and that timing is still shaky. Tomorrow afternoon is your best window to get outside.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Low clouds remain stubbornly entrenched across portions of northern and eastern VT this afternoon, while other areas are finally experiencing some sunshine. Cloud cover should continue to slowly erode as we head into this evening. However, expect clouds will return overnight, particularly over the Adirondacks as moisture from the Great Lakes becomes trapped under the inversion. Otherwise, expect drier and warmer conditions through at least mid week as ridging settles over the eastern CONUS. Each day will likely see partly to mostly sunny skies, with each afternoon a few degrees warmer than the previous one; highs will reach well into the 50s in most spots by Wednesday/Thursday. Nighttime temperatures will be seasonable, generally in the 30s, though some of the colder hollows in the Northeast Kingdom and Adirondacks may dip into the upper 20s. KEY MESSAGE 2: The stretch of warm and dry weather will continue into the second half of the week and into the weekend as deep upper level ridging and surface high pressure remains in places over the eastern United States. The surface high looks to be centered to our south Thursday, gradually shifting northeastward towards the weekend. The latest model guidance shows the ridge gradually down towards the weekend, with a cold front possibly bringing some showers Sunday into Monday, although some guidance shows a stronger low well to our south with our region remaining dry. There is still a lot of uncertainty regarding the pattern at that time frame, especially in regards to how quickly the ridge begins to weaken and the actual pattern evolution, but currently late this weekend looks to be the next chances of any precipitation for the region. Temperatures during this time frame will continue to be on the warm side, with highs in the 50s to near 60 late this week into the weekend.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - After our first widespread taste of wintry weather across the region this weekend, a stretch of dry and mild November weather is taking shape across Vermont and the North Country. Clouds will continue to break up this evening, with plenty of sunshine in the forecast through the week. Highs will climb into the 50s, while nights remain chilly. Our next chance for a few showers arrives late Sunday, though the timing is still uncertain. Saturday looks mostly sunny, with a high of 55° and an overnight low of 46°. Sunday will be partly sunny and breezy, with a high of 56° and gusts up to 26 mph. A few scattered showers are possible Sunday night, with a low of 43°. The timing and extent of any showers remain uncertain. Monday turns cooler and partly sunny, with a high of 46°.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-16T18:14:00Z — same caveat): Staying chilly, but the sun emerges Monday afternoon — Clouds give way to more breaks of sun Monday afternoon, especially away from the Northeast Kingdom. It stays cooler than average, with highs in the low 40s. High pressure continues to build in tonight, so the sky turns mostly clear. It will be seasonably cold, with lows in the 20s to around 30. Tuesday marks the transition toward brighter and warmer weather. Expect a partly to mostly sunny sky, with highs reaching the low to mid-50s. The Wednesday through Friday stretch looks beautiful, with partly sunny skies and highs in the upper 50s to low 60s! The quiet pattern continues this weekend, as it stays mostly dry with partial sunshine and highs reaching the upper 50s. A cold front may bring a round of showers and a few snowflakes late Sunday into Monday, sending in more seasonable air for early Thanksgiving week. Highs fall back closer to 40.
